indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B5.1.1.3 Demonstrate an understanding of factors, multiples of numbers including composite, even, odd and prime numbers from 1 to 100
indicator.objective: Generate and identify prime numbers and composite numbers between 1 and 100

skills.description: Identify prime and composite numbers between 1 and 100.
Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to find primes up to 100.
Explain why a number is prime or composite (e.g., number of factors).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Thinking all odd numbers are prime (e.g., 9, 15, 21).

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is prime?
hints: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
7 has factors 1 and 7 only.
questions.explanation: 7 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 7.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is composite?
hints: Composite numbers have more than two factors.
questions.explanation: 8 is composite because it has factors 1, 2, 4, 8.

questions.stem: Why is 1 NOT a prime number?
hints: Prime numbers must have exactly two factors.
questions.explanation: 1 has only one factor (itself), so it is not prime.
questions.misconception: Thinking 1 is prime because it seems like a basic number.

questions.stem: What is the smallest prime number?
hints: It is the only even prime.
questions.explanation: 2 is the smallest prime number.

questions.stem: Is 2 a prime number?
options: Yes, because it has exactly two factors: 1 and 2.
No, because it is too small.
hints: Check its factors.
questions.explanation: 2 is prime; it is the only even prime number.
questions.misconception: Thinking all even numbers are composite.

questions.stem: List all the prime numbers between 1 and 20.
hints: Check each number for factors.
questions.explanation: The primes between 1 and 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.

questions.stem: What is the only even prime number?
hints: All other even numbers are divisible by 2.
questions.explanation: 2 is the only even prime.

questions.stem: Explain why 12 is a composite number.
hints: List its factors.
questions.explanation: 12 is composite because it has more than two factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

criteria.description: States that 12 has more than two factors.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is NOT prime?
hints: 15 has factors 1, 3, 5, 15.
questions.explanation: 15 is composite because it has more than two factors.
questions.misconception: Thinking all odd numbers are prime.

questions.stem: List all the composite numbers between 1 and 10.
hints: Composite numbers have more than 2 factors.
questions.explanation: The composite numbers between 1 and 10 are 4, 6, 8, 9, 10.

questions.stem: In the Sieve of Eratosthenes, which number is crossed out first?
hints: 1 is not prime, so it is crossed out first.
questions.explanation: 1 is crossed out first because it is not prime.

questions.stem: Explain how the Sieve of Eratosthenes works.
hints: Cross out multiples of primes starting from 2.
questions.explanation: You write numbers 1 to 100. Cross out 1. Then cross out multiples of 2 (except 2), then multiples of 3 (except 3), then 5, then 7, etc. The numbers not crossed out are prime.

criteria.description: States the remaining numbers are prime.

questions.misconception: Thinking it is a random process.

questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 30?
questions.explanation: There are 10 prime numbers between 1 and 30.

questions.stem: Which of these is a prime number?
hints: 31 has only factors 1 and 31.
questions.explanation: 31 is prime.
questions.misconception: Choosing 21, 27, or 33 because they are odd.

questions.stem: Explain why 91 is a composite number, even though it looks like it might be prime.
hints: Try dividing 91 by 7.
questions.explanation: 91 is composite because 7 × 13 = 91. So its factors are 1, 7, 13, 91.

criteria.description: Concludes it has more than two factors.

questions.misconception: Thinking 91 is prime because it is not divisible by 2, 3, or 5.

questions.stem: List all the prime numbers between 50 and 70.
hints: Check each number for factors.
questions.explanation: The primes between 50 and 70 are 53, 59, 61, 67.

questions.stem: A pupil says 'All odd numbers are prime.' Give three odd numbers that are composite to prove the pupil wrong.
hints: Think of odd numbers with more than two factors.
questions.explanation: 9 (factors 1,3,9), 15 (1,3,5,15), 21 (1,3,7,21) are odd composite numbers.
questions.misconception: Believing all odd numbers are prime.

questions.stem: A pupil says 1 is prime because it only has 1 and itself as factors. Explain why this is incorrect.
hints: Prime numbers must have exactly two distinct factors.
questions.explanation: 1 does not have two distinct factors; its only factor is 1. So it is not prime.

criteria.description: Explains prime needs exactly two factors.

questions.stem: What is the largest prime number less than 100?
hints: Check each number for factors.
questions.explanation: 97 is the largest prime under 100.

questions.stem: After crossing out multiples of 2, 3, and 5, which numbers remain in the first row (1-10) of the Sieve of Eratosthenes?
hints: 1 is crossed out first. 4, 6, 8, 10 are multiples of 2. 9 is a multiple of 3.
questions.explanation: The remaining numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7.
